translations.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,
To the church of God in Corinth, the called and holy people who are sanctified in Jesus Christ, and to all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, theirs and ours.
Grace and peace be with you from God our Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God for you because of the grace of God given to you in Jesus Christ.
For in him you have become rich in everything, in all speech and all knowledge,
just as the testimony about Christ was confirmed among you,
so that you lack none of his gifts, but are waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
He will strengthen you until the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful, through whom you were called into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

Now I ask you, my brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak in agreement and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be fully united in the same mind and the same judgment.
For people from Chloe’s household have sent me word about you, my brothers, that there are quarrels among you.
What I mean is this: some of you say, “I belong to Paul,” others say, “I belong to Apollos,” others say, “I belong to Cephas,” and others say, “I belong to Christ.”
Has Christ been divided? Or was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in Paul’s name?
I thank my God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
so that no one can say that I baptized in my own name.
I also baptized the household of Stephanas. Beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.
For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the good news—not with wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ would not be emptied of its power.
For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and frustrate the understanding of the discerning.”
Where is the wise person? Or where is the scribe? Or where is the debater of this world? Has not God made the wisdom of this world foolish?
For since, in God’s wisdom, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was pleased to save those who believe through the foolishness of preaching.
For Jews ask for signs, and Gentiles seek wisdom.
But we proclaim Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
but to those who are called, both Jews and Gentiles, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For God’s foolishness is wiser than human beings, and God’s weakness is stronger than human beings.
Consider your calling, my brothers: not many of you are wise by human standards, not many of you are powerful, and not many of you come from noble families.
But God chose the foolish people of the world to shame the wise, and he chose the weak people of the world to shame the powerful.
And he chose those of low birth in the world, the despised, and those who are nothing, to bring to nothing those who are something.
So that no human being might boast before him.
But it is because of him that you are in Jesus Christ, who became for us wisdom from God, righteousness, holiness, and redemption.
As it is written: Whoever boasts should boast in the Lord.
And when I came to you, my brothers, I did not proclaim God's mystery to you with impressive speech or wisdom.
I did not consider myself to know anything among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
And I was with you in great fear and trembling.
My speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in a demonstration of the Spirit and of power,
so that your faith would not rest on human wisdom, but on God's power.
Yet we speak wisdom among the mature, but not the wisdom of this world or of the rulers of this world, who are being brought to nothing.
Instead, we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom that was hidden and that God had appointed before the ages for our glory.
None of the rulers of this world knew it, for if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
But as it is written: "No eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived what God has prepared for those who love him."
But God has revealed it to us through his Spirit, for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
For who knows what is within a person except that person's own spirit within them? In the same way, no one knows what is within God except God's Spirit.
But we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we might know the gifts that have been given to us by God.
We also speak of these things, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in the teaching of the Spirit, interpreting spiritual things for spiritual people.
For the unspiritual person does not accept spiritual things, because they are foolishness to that person, who cannot understand them because they are discerned through the Spirit.
But the spiritual person discerns everything, yet is judged by no one.
For who has known the mind of the Lord so that he might teach him? But we have the mind of Christ.
And I, my brothers, could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as people ruled by the body, as infants in Christ.
I gave you milk to drink and did not give you solid food, because you were not yet able to take it. Indeed, even now you are not able.
For you are still living according to the flesh. Since there are jealousy, strife, and divisions among you, are you not people ruled by the body, living according to the flesh?
For when one of you says, "I belong to Paul," and another says, "I belong to Apollos," are you not people ruled by the body?
For who is Paul, or who is Apollos, except servants through whom you believed, each as the Lord granted him?
I planted, and Apollos watered, but God made it grow.
So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but God is the one who makes things grow.
The one who plants and the one who waters are one, and each will receive a reward according to his labor.
For we work with God, and you are God's cultivated field and God's building.
According to the grace of God given to me, I laid a foundation like a wise master builder, and another person is building on it. But each person should take care how he builds on it.
For no one can lay any other foundation besides the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
Now if anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,
everyone’s work will be revealed. For that day will expose it, because it is revealed by fire, and the fire will test what each person’s work is like.
If anyone’s work endures, the one who built it will receive his reward.
If anyone’s work is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself, however, will be saved, but as though escaping from fire.
Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit lives in you?
Whoever destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him. For God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.
Let no one deceive himself. Whoever among you thinks he is wise in this world must become a fool so that he may become wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness before God. For it is written, “He catches the wise in their own cunning.”
And again, “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are empty.”
Therefore, let no one boast about human beings, for everything is yours.
Whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, or the world or life or death, or present things or things to come—everything is yours.
And you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
This is how you should regard us: as servants of Christ and stewards of God’s mysteries.
Now what is required of stewards is that each one be found faithful.
But to me it matters very little whether I am judged by you or by any human being. In fact, I do not even judge myself.
For I am aware of nothing against myself, but that does not make me righteous. It is the Lord who judges me.
Therefore, do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes. He brings to light the things hidden in darkness and reveals the thoughts of hearts. Then each person will receive praise from God.

Now, my brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that through us you may learn not to think beyond what is written, and so that none of you may become arrogant toward another on account of any person.
For who makes you different? Or what do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?
You are already full and have become rich! You have become kings without us! I wish you really had become kings, so that we too might reign with you.
For I think God has placed us apostles last, like people condemned to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, to angels, and to human beings.
We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are disgraced.
To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty, poorly clothed and beaten, and we have no settled home.
We toil, working with our own hands. When people insult us, we bless them. When they persecute us, we endure it.
When they slander us, we appeal to them. We have become like the refuse of the world, the scrapings of everyone, right up to now.
I am not writing these things to shame you, but to admonish you as beloved children.
For even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. For in Jesus Christ I became your father through the gospel.
Therefore I ask you to imitate me.
For this reason I sent Timothy to you. He is my beloved son and is faithful in the Lord. He will remind you of my ways in Christ, just as I teach in all the churches.
But some of you have become arrogant, as though I were not coming to you.
But if the Lord wills, I will come to you soon, and I will find out not what these arrogant people say, but what power they have.
For the kingdom of God is not a matter of words, but of power.
What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod, or with love and a gentle spirit?
It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and sexual immorality of a kind not even named among the pagans: a son has taken his father's wife.
Yet you are arrogant! Should you not instead have mourned, so that the man who did this would be removed from among you?
For although I am far from you in body, I am near you in spirit, and I have already judged the man who did this, as though I were present.
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, all of you are to gather together, with me present with you in spirit, and with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
and hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of his body, so that he may live in the spirit on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven makes the whole batch of dough rise?
Clean out the old leaven from among you, so that you may be a new batch of dough, just as you are unleavened. For our Passover sacrifice is Christ, who was slaughtered for us.
Therefore let us celebrate the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of wickedness and bitterness, but with the leaven of purity and holiness.
I wrote to you in the letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.
But I do not mean the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy, or robbers, or idol worshipers. Otherwise, you would have to leave the world altogether.

Rather, what I wrote to you was not to associate with anyone who is called a brother but is sexually immoral, greedy, an idol worshiper, verbally abusive, a drunkard, or a robber. Do not even eat bread with such a person.
For what have I to do with judging outsiders? You are to judge those inside.
But God judges outsiders. Remove the evil person from among you.
Does anyone among you, when he has a dispute with his brother, dare to go to court before the unrighteous rather than before the holy ones?
Or do you not know that the holy ones will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unfit to judge minor cases?
Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more, then, the matters of this world!
But if you have a case concerning worldly matters, appoint as your judges those who are least esteemed in the church.
I say this to shame you. Is there not even one wise person among you who can settle a dispute between one brother and another?
Instead, a brother goes to court against his brother, and before unbelievers at that!
So you have already defeated yourselves by having lawsuits against one another. Why not rather suffer wrong? Why not rather let yourselves be cheated?
Instead, you yourselves do wrong and cheat—even your own brothers.

Or do you not know that the wicked will not inherit God's kingdom? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idol worshipers, nor adulterers, nor the sexually corrupt, nor men who sleep with males.
Nor will greedy people, thieves, drunkards, those who insult others, or robbers inherit the kingdom of God.
And some of you were like that. But you were washed, you were made holy, and you were made righteous in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
Everything is permitted for me, but not everything benefits me. Everything is permitted for me, but I will let no one gain mastery over me.
Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for food, but God will do away with both. The body, however, is not for sexual immorality but for our Lord, and our Lord is for the body.
God raised our Lord and will also raise us by his power.
Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Should we take a member of Christ and make it a member of a prostitute? Certainly not!
Or do you not know that whoever joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her? For it is said, “The two will become one body.”
But whoever joins himself to our Lord becomes one spirit with him.
Flee from sexual immorality. Every sin a person commits is outside his body, but whoever commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who lives in you, whom you received from God, and that you do not belong to yourselves?
For you were bought at a price. Therefore, glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which belong to God.
Now concerning the things you wrote to me about: it is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman.
But because of sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman should have her own husband.
A husband should fulfill the marital obligation he owes his wife, and likewise the wife should fulfill hers to her husband.
A wife does not have authority over her own body, but her husband does. Likewise, a husband does not have authority over his own body, but his wife does.

So do not deprive one another, except when you both agree for a time, so that you can devote yourselves to fasting and prayer. Then return to marital relations, so that Satan does not tempt you because of your bodily desire.
But I say this as to those who are weak, not as a command.
For I wish that everyone were like me in chastity. But each person has been given a gift from God, one in this way and another in that.
But I say to those who have no wives and to widows that it is good for them to remain as I am.
But if they cannot restrain themselves, let them marry. For it is much better to take a wife than to burn with desire.
To those who have wives I give this command—not I, but my Lord: a wife must not separate from her husband.
But if she does separate, she must remain without a husband or be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.
To the rest I say—I, not my Lord—if a brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.
And if a woman has an unbelieving husband, and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce her husband.

For the unbelieving husband is made holy through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is made holy through her believing husband. Otherwise their children would be unclean, but as it is, they are clean.
But if the unbeliever separates, let that person separate. A brother or sister is not bound in such circumstances. God has called us to peace.
For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or do you, husband, know whether you will save your wife?
Rather, let each person live according to what the Lord has allotted to them and as God has called them. This is also what I command in all the churches.
If someone was circumcised when called, he should not reverse it and become uncircumcised. And if someone was uncircumcised when called, he should not be circumcised.
For circumcision is nothing, and neither is uncircumcision, but keeping God's commandments is what matters.
Let each person remain in the calling in which they were called.
Were you called as a slave? Do not let it trouble you. But even if you can become free, choose to serve.
For anyone who was called in our Lord as a slave is God's freed person. Likewise, anyone who was called as a free person is Christ's slave.
You were bought for a price. Do not become slaves of human beings.
My brothers, let each person remain with God in the condition in which they were called.
Now concerning virginity, I have no command from God, but I give advice as someone who has received mercy from God to be trustworthy.
I think this is good because of the distress of the present time: it is beneficial for a person to remain as they are.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you free from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
But if you marry a wife, you do not sin, and if a virgin marries a man, she does not sin. Yet those who do so will experience bodily distress, and I want to spare you.
This is what I say, my brothers: from now on, time has grown short. Those who have wives should be as though they had none.
Those who weep should be as though they did not weep; those who rejoice, as though they did not rejoice; and those who buy, as though they did not possess.
Those who use this world should not go beyond its proper use, for the present form of this world is passing away.
For this reason I want you to be free from anxiety. For the man who has no wife is concerned with his Lord's affairs, with how to please his Lord.
But the man who has a wife is concerned with the world's affairs, with how to please his wife.

There is also a difference between a married woman and a virgin. The woman who has not married a man is concerned with her Lord, so that she may be holy in her body and in her spirit. But the woman who has a husband is concerned with the world's affairs, with how to please her husband.
I say this for your own benefit. I am not putting a noose around you, but want you to remain devoted to your Lord in a fitting way, without being preoccupied with the world.

But if anyone thinks he is being disgraced because his virgin daughter has passed the age for marriage and he has not given her to a husband, and that he ought to give her in marriage, let him do as he wishes. He is not sinning. Let her marry.
But whoever has firmly decided in his mind, is under no compulsion, has control over his own will, and has resolved in his heart to keep his daughter unmarried does well.
So whoever gives his virgin daughter in marriage does well, and whoever does not give his virgin daughter in marriage does even better.
A woman is bound by the law as long as her husband lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry whomever she wishes, only in our Lord.
But she is happier if she remains as she is, according to my own judgment. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God in me.
Now concerning sacrifices offered to idols: we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge makes people arrogant, but love builds up.
But if anyone thinks he knows something, he does not yet know anything as he ought to know it.
But if anyone loves God, that person is known by him.
So concerning the eating of sacrifices offered to idols: we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God but one.
For even if there are those called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—as there are many gods and many lords—
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom everything comes, and we are in him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom everything exists, and we too exist through him.

But not everyone has this knowledge. For some people, whose consciences are still concerned with idols, eat the food as something sacrificed to an idol. And because their conscience is weak, it is defiled.
But food does not bring us closer to God. We are no better off if we eat, and no worse off if we do not eat.
But take care that this freedom of yours does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
For if someone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining at a meal in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, because he is weak, be encouraged to eat what has been sacrificed?
And through your knowledge that weak person, for whom Christ died, is ruined.
And if you sin against your brothers in this way and wound their weak consciences, you are sinning against Christ.
Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat, so that I do not cause my brother to stumble.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in my Lord?
Even if I am not an apostle to others, I am to you. You are the seal of my apostleship.
This is my defense to those who judge me.
Do we not have the right to eat and drink?
And do we not have the right to take along a believing wife, as the other apostles do, and as our Lord's brothers and Cephas do?
Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no right to refrain from working?
Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Or who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Or who tends a flock and does not consume milk from his flock?
Am I saying these things merely from a human point of view? Look, the law also says these things.
For it is written in the law of Moses, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.” Is God concerned about oxen?
Surely he said this for our sake. For it was written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the one who threshes ought to do so in hope of a harvest.
If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?
If others have this right over you, are we not entitled to it even more? But we have not used this right. Instead, we endure everything so that we do not hinder the good news of Christ in any way.
Do you not know that those who serve in the temple receive their support from the temple, and those who serve at the altar share in what is offered on the altar?
In the same way, our Lord also commanded that those who proclaim his good news should make their living from his good news.
But I have not used any of these rights. Nor have I written this so that this should be done for me. For I would rather die than have anyone make my boasting empty.
For even when I proclaim the good news, I have nothing to boast about, because I am under compulsion. Woe to me if I do not proclaim the good news!
For if I do this willingly, I have a reward. But if unwillingly, I have still been entrusted with a stewardship.
What, then, is my reward? That when I proclaim the good news, I make the good news of Christ available free of charge, without using the right given to me in the gospel.
For although I am free from everything, I have made myself a slave to everyone so that I might win many.
Among the Jews I became like a Jew so that I might win the Jews. Among those who are under the law, I became like someone under the law so that I might win those who are under the law.
To those who have no law, I became like someone without law—though I am not without God's law, but under Christ's law—so that I might also win those who are without law.
Among the weak I became like someone weak so that I might win the weak. I became everything to everyone so that I might save everyone.
I do this so that I may share in the good news.
Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.
Everyone who competes exercises self-control in everything. They run to receive a crown that perishes, but we run to receive one that does not perish.
So I run with a definite goal, not toward something unknown. And I fight, not like someone punching the air.
Instead, I discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest, after proclaiming to others, I myself should be rejected.
Now I want you to know, my brothers, that our ancestors were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea.
And all were baptized through Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
And all ate the same spiritual food.
And all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that went with them, and that rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, for they fell in the wilderness.
Now these things became examples for us, so that we would not desire evil things as they did.
Nor should we worship idols, as some of them did. As it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to play.”
Nor should we commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
We should not put Christ to the test, as some of them did, and snakes destroyed them.
And do not grumble, as some of them grumbled and perished at the hands of the destroyer.
Now all these things that happened to them served as examples for us. They were written for our instruction, upon whom the end of the ages has come.
So whoever thinks he is standing should take care not to fall.

No temptation has reached you except what is common to human beings. But God is faithful: he will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear. Instead, he will provide a way out of your temptation, so that you can endure it.
Therefore, my dear friends, flee from the worship of idols.
I am speaking to you as wise people. Judge for yourselves what I say.
The cup of thanksgiving that we bless—is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? And the bread that we break—is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?
Just as that bread is one, so we are all one body, for we all partake of that one bread.
Look at Israel according to the flesh. Do not those who eat the sacrifices share in the altar?
What, then, am I saying? That an idol is anything, or that a sacrifice offered to an idol is anything? No.
Rather, what pagans sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. And I do not want you to become partners with demons.
You cannot drink the cup of our Lord and the cup of demons. And you cannot share in the table of our Lord and the table of demons.
Or are we provoking our Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he is?
Everything is permitted to me, but not everything is beneficial. Everything is permitted to me, but not everything builds up.
No one should seek his own good alone, but everyone should also seek the good of his neighbor.
Eat whatever is sold in the meat market, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.
For the earth and everything in it belong to the Lord.
If one of the pagans invites you and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.
But if someone tells you, “This has been offered in sacrifice,” do not eat it, for the sake of the person who told you and for the sake of conscience.
By conscience, I mean not your own, but that of the person who told you. For why should my freedom be judged by another person's conscience?
If I partake with thanksgiving, why am I denounced for something for which I give thanks?
So whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.
Do not be a stumbling block to Jews, to Gentiles, or to the church of God.
Just as I too please everyone in everything, not seeking what benefits me but what benefits the many, so that they may live.
Imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.
Now I praise you, my brothers, because you remember me in everything and hold to the instructions just as I handed them on to you.
But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for she is the same as a woman whose head is shaved.
For if a woman does not cover herself, let her also have her hair cut off. But if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or shaved, let her cover herself.
For a man ought not to cover his head, because he is the likeness and glory of God. But a woman is the glory of man.
For man is not from woman, but woman from man.
Nor was man created for the sake of woman, but woman for the sake of man.
For this reason a woman must have authority over her head, because of the angels.
Nevertheless, in our Lord, neither is man independent of woman nor woman independent of man.
For just as woman is from man, so man also comes through woman. But everything is from God.
Judge for yourselves among yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Does not nature itself teach you that when a man lets his hair grow long, it is a disgrace to him?
But when a woman grows her hair long, it is her glory, because her hair has been given to her as a covering.
But if anyone argues about these things, we have no such custom, nor does the church of God.
In giving you this instruction, I am not praising you, because you have not moved forward but have declined.
For first of all, when you gather in the church, I hear that there are divisions among you, and I believe it to some extent.
For disputes are also bound to arise among you, so that those among you who have proved themselves may be recognized.
So when you gather, you do not eat and drink in a way that is fitting for our Lord’s day.
Instead, each person goes ahead and eats his own supper, and one is hungry while another is drunk.
Do you not have houses in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? I do not praise you.
For I received from our Lord what I also handed on to you: that our Lord Jesus, on the night when he was being betrayed, took bread,
and blessed it and broke it, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Keep doing this in remembrance of me.”
Likewise, after they had eaten supper, he also gave the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Keep doing this, whenever you drink, in remembrance of me.”
For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you commemorate the death of our Lord until he comes.
Therefore, whoever eats the Lord’s bread and drinks from his cup without being worthy of it is guilty concerning the Lord’s blood and body.
For this reason, a person should examine himself, and then eat this bread and drink from this cup.
For whoever eats and drinks from it unworthily eats and drinks condemnation on himself, because he does not recognize the Lord’s body.
For this reason, many among you are sick and weak, and many are asleep [?].
For if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.
But when we are judged by our Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.
So then, my brothers, when you gather to eat, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that your gathering does not bring condemnation. As for the remaining matters, I will give you instructions when I come.
Now concerning spiritual gifts, my brothers, I want you to know:
You were pagans, and you were led without discernment to idols that have no voice.
For this reason, I make known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus is cursed.” Nor can anyone say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the Spirit is one.
There are different kinds of service, but the Lord is one.
And there are different kinds of mighty works, but God is one, and he brings about everything in everyone.
To each person a manifestation of the Spirit is given in a way that benefits him.
To one, a message of wisdom is given through the Spirit; to another, a message of knowledge through the same Spirit.
To another, faith through the same Spirit; to another, gifts of healing through the same Spirit.
To another, mighty works; to another, prophecy; to another, discernment of spirits; to another, various kinds of tongues; to another, interpretation of tongues.
But one Spirit does all these things, distributing them to each person as the Spirit wishes.
For just as the body is one and has many parts, and all the parts of the body, though many, are one body, so also is Christ.
For we too were all baptized by one Spirit into one body, whether Jews or Gentiles, slaves or free. And we all drank of one Spirit.
For the body is not one part, but many.
For if the foot says, “Because I am not a hand, I am not part of the body,” that does not make it cease to be part of the body.
And if the ear says, “Because I am not an eye, I am not part of the body,” that does not make it cease to be part of the body.
For if the whole body were eyes, where would hearing be? And if it were all hearing, how would it smell?
But as it is, God has placed each of the parts in the body just as he wished.
But if they were all one part, where would the body be?
Now there are many parts, but one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”
Rather, those parts that seem weak are all the more necessary.
And those parts of the body that we consider less honorable, we give greater honor. Those parts that require modesty, we treat with greater decency.
But the honorable parts we have need no honor. For God has put the body together and given greater honor to the lesser part,
so that there should be no division in the body, but all the parts should care equally for one another.
Whenever one part is in pain, all of them suffer. And if one part is honored, all the parts share in that honor.
Now you are Christ's body, and each of you is a part in your own place.

For God has appointed in his church first apostles, after them prophets, after them teachers, after them workers of miracles, after them gifts of healing, and helpers, leaders, and various kinds of languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in languages? Or do all interpret?
But if you are eager for the greater gifts, I will also show you a more excellent way.
If I speak in every language of human beings and in those of angels, but have no love in me, I have become a resounding gong or a clanging cymbal.
And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so that I can move a mountain, but have no love in me, I am nothing.
And if I use everything I have to feed the poor, and if I hand over my body to be burned, but have no love in me, I gain nothing.
Love is patient and kind. Love does not envy. Love is not agitated and does not become arrogant.
It does not act shamefully or seek its own interests. It is not provoked and does not think evil.
It does not rejoice in injustice, but rejoices in the truth.
It bears everything, believes everything, hopes for everything, and endures everything.
Love never fails. For prophecies will come to an end, languages will fall silent, and knowledge will come to an end.
For we know only a little out of much, and we prophesy only a little out of much.
But when completeness comes, then what was partial will come to an end.
When I was a child, I spoke like a child, thought like a child, and reasoned like a child. But when I became a man, I put an end to childish things.
Now we see as in a mirror, in a riddle, but then face to face. Now I know a little out of much, but then I will know just as I have been known.
For these are the three things that remain: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of them is love.
Pursue love, and eagerly desire the gifts of the Spirit, especially that you may prophesy.
For someone who speaks in a tongue speaks not to people but to God. No one understands what he says, but in the spirit he speaks mysteries.
But someone who prophesies speaks to people to build them up, encourage them, and comfort them.
Someone who speaks in a tongue builds himself up, but someone who prophesies builds up the church.

I want all of you to speak in tongues, but even more, I want you to prophesy. For someone who prophesies is greater than someone who speaks in a tongue, unless he interprets. But if he interprets, he builds up the church.
Now, my brothers, if I come to you and speak with you in tongues, how will I benefit you unless I speak to you with revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?

Even lifeless things that make a sound, whether a flute or a lyre, must distinguish one note from another. Otherwise, how can anyone recognize what is being played on the flute or plucked on the strings?
And if a horn sounds an indistinct call, who will prepare for battle?
So it is with you: if you say something in a tongue and it is not interpreted, how will anyone understand what you are saying? You will be like people speaking to the air.
For there are indeed many kinds of languages in the world, and not one of them is without sound.
But if I do not know the meaning of the sound, I will be a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker will be a foreigner to me.
So also you, since you are eager for the gifts of the Spirit, should seek to excel in building up the church.
And someone who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind bears no fruit.
What, then, should I do? I will pray with my spirit, and I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, and I will also sing with my mind.
Otherwise, if you offer a blessing in the spirit, how can someone in the position of an unlearned person say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
For you offer a blessing well, but your companion is not built up.
I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
But in the church I would rather speak five words with my mind, so that I may also teach others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
My brothers, do not be children in your thinking. Rather, be infants when it comes to evil, but be mature in your thinking.
It is written in the law: “With foreign speech and in another tongue I will speak to this people. Yet even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.”
So tongues are appointed as a sign, not for believers but for unbelievers. Prophecies, however, are not for unbelievers but for believers.
So if the whole church gathers together and everyone speaks in tongues, and unlearned people or unbelievers come in, will they not say that these people have gone mad?
But if you are all prophesying, and an untrained person or an unbeliever comes among you, he is examined by all of you and convicted by all of you.
The secrets of his heart are revealed. Then he will fall on his face and worship God, saying, “God is truly among you.”

So I say, my brothers, whenever you gather, whoever among you has a psalm should speak, as should whoever has a teaching, whoever has a revelation, whoever has a tongue, and whoever has an interpretation. Let everything be done to build one another up.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, let two speak, or at most three. Let them speak one at a time, and let one person interpret.
If there is no interpreter, let the person who speaks in a tongue remain silent in the church and speak privately to himself and to God.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others evaluate.
If something is revealed to another who is sitting there, let the first speaker become silent.
For you can all prophesy one at a time, so that everyone may learn and everyone may be encouraged.
For the spirit of the prophets is subject to the prophets.
For God is not a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints.
Let your women remain silent in the church, for they are not permitted to speak, but must be subject, as the law also says.
If they want to learn anything, let them ask their husbands at home, for it is shameful for women to speak in the church.
Or did the word of God originate with you? Or did it reach you alone?
If anyone among you thinks that he is a prophet or a spiritual person, let him recognize that the things I am writing to you are commands of our Lord.
But if anyone does not recognize this, let him remain ignorant.
So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
But let everything be done properly and in order.
Now I make known to you, my brothers, the good news that I preached to you, which you received and in which you stand.
Through it you are also saved, if you remember the message I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.
For at the outset I handed on to you what I had received: that Christ died for our sins, as it is written;
that he was buried and rose on the third day, as it is written;
and that he appeared to Cephas, and afterward to the Twelve.
After that he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, many of whom are still alive, though some have fallen asleep.
After these things he appeared to James, and afterward to all the apostles.
Last of all, he appeared also to me, as to one born before the proper time.
For I am the least of the apostles, and I am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
But by God's grace I am what I am, and his grace in me was not wasted. Instead, I worked harder than all of them—yet not I, but his grace that was with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
But if Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, how can some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not risen either.
And if Christ has not risen, our preaching is empty, and your faith is also empty.
We are also found to be false witnesses about God, because we testified about God that he raised Christ, when he did not raise him.
For if the dead do not rise, then Christ has not risen either.
And if Christ has not risen, your faith is futile, and you are still in your sins.
Then those who have fallen asleep in Christ have also perished.
And if we hope in Christ only in this life, we are more pitiable than all other people.
But now Christ has risen from the dead and has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
And just as death came through a human being, so also the resurrection of the dead comes through a human being.
For just as all people die in Adam, so also all will live in Christ.
Each in their own order: Christ became the firstfruits; afterward, at his coming, those who belong to Christ.
Then the end will come, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he has abolished every ruler, every authority, and every power.
For he is to reign until he puts all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be abolished is death.
For he subjected everything under his feet. But when he says that everything is subjected to him, it is clear that this excludes the one who subjected everything to him.
And when everything has been subjected to him, then the Son himself will be subjected to the one who subjected everything to him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what will those who are baptized on behalf of the dead do? If the dead do not rise, why are they baptized on behalf of the dead?
And why do we also stand in danger every hour?
I swear, my brothers, by the pride I have in you in our Lord Jesus Christ, that I die every day.
If, in human terms, I was thrown to wild beasts in Ephesus, what did I gain if the dead do not rise? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Do not be deceived: evil conversations corrupt good minds.
Awaken your hearts to righteousness, and do not sin. For there are some who have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
Someone among you will say, "How do the dead rise, and with what kind of body do they come?"
You fool! The seed you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
What you sow is not the body that is to be, but a bare grain of wheat or barley or some other seed.
But God gives it a body as he wishes, and to each seed a body of its own nature.
But not all bodies are alike. The human body is one kind, the body of an animal another, the body of a bird another, and the body of a fish another.
There are heavenly bodies, and there are earthly bodies. But the glory of the heavenly bodies is one kind, and that of the earthly bodies is another.
The sun has one glory, the moon another glory, and the stars another glory. And one star surpasses another in glory.
So it is also with the resurrection of the dead. They are sown subject to decay; they rise free from decay.
They are sown in dishonor; they rise in glory. They are sown in weakness; they rise in power.
A natural body is sown; a spiritual body rises. For there is a body of the soul, and there is a body of the spirit.
So it is also written: “Adam, the first man, became a living soul,” and the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
But the spiritual did not come first; rather, the natural came first, and then the spiritual.
The first man was made of dust, from the earth; the second man is the Lord from heaven.
As the one made of dust is, so also are those made of dust. And as the one from heaven is, so also are those who are heavenly.
And just as we have worn the likeness of the one made of dust, so we will wear the likeness of the one from heaven.
Now I say this, my brothers: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of heaven, nor does decay inherit freedom from decay.
Look, I tell you a mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
swiftly, in the blink of an eye, when the last trumpet sounds. The dead will rise free from decay, and we will be changed.
For this body that decays is to put on freedom from decay, and this body that dies is to put on immortality.
But when this body that decays puts on freedom from decay, and this body that dies puts on immortality, then the saying that is written will come true: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
Where is your sting, death? Or where is your victory, Sheol?
Now the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who has given us victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, my brothers and loved ones, be firm and do not be shaken. Instead, always excel in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
Now concerning what is being collected for the saints: do as I instructed the churches of Galatia.
On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside and keep at home whatever he can spare from what he receives, so that collections will not have to be made when I come.
And when I come, I will send those whom you choose with a letter to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
But if the matter warrants my going as well, they will go with me.
I will come to you after I have passed through Macedonia, for I am going to pass through Macedonia.
Perhaps I will stay with you, or even spend the winter with you, so that you may send me on my way wherever I go.
For I do not want to see you now merely while passing through. I hope to stay with you for some time, if my Lord permits me.
But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost.
For a great door, full of opportunities for work, has opened for me, and there are many opponents.
If Timothy comes to you, see that he has nothing to fear among you, for he does the Lord’s work just as I do.
So let no one despise him. Instead, send him on his way in peace so that he may come to me, for I am expecting him with the brothers.
As for Apollos, my brothers, I urged him strongly to come to you with the brothers. But apparently he was not willing to come to you. When he has an opportunity, he will come to you.
Be watchful and stand firm in the faith. Be courageous and strong.
Let everything you do be done in love.
Now I appeal to you, my brothers, concerning the household of Stephanas. You know that they were the first converts in Achaia and that they have devoted themselves to serving the saints.
You too should submit to people like these, and to everyone who labors with us and helps.
I rejoice at the arrival of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, because they have supplied what was lacking from you toward me.
For they have refreshed my spirit and yours. So give recognition to people like these.
All the churches in Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Priscilla, together with the church in their house, send you warm greetings in our Lord.
All our brothers send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
This greeting is in my own handwriting—Paul’s.
If anyone does not love our Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Our Lord has come.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
And my love is with all of you in Christ Jesus.
